note.p: See Ed Pope's note: A Dr Burke of the United Irishmen stood bail along with the Hon Simon Butler Dict Irish Biog 1757-1797 for Archibald Hamilton Rowan when he was arrested in 1792 and a Dr Burke was one of the Catholic gentlemen arrested in August 1811 for contravening the Convention Act along with Dr Edward Sheridan who was acquitted and Thomas Kirwan Dict Irish Biog 1772-1852. J T Burke of Arran Quay Dublin was a physician to the Charitable Dispensary Meath St in 1792 and the Dr Burke who stood bail for Rowan was said by W P Carey to have been a learned physician. Assuming the 1792 and 1811 Burkes were the same it is astonishing that he cannot be found in any biographical sources. At the meeting in 1811 for which they were prosecuted Dr Burke took the chair when Dr Sheridan had to stand down.
